as_extracts.name: LITAF102-E08
as_extracts.description: They begin to explain their understanding of the features and grammatical structures of Italian using simple metalanguage.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2U03 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: recognise and explore how the Roman alphabet and features of language are used to construct meaning in Italian

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating the pronunciation of the 21 letters of the Italian alphabet by singing along with the online video of the Italian alphabet song

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that the letters j, k, w, x and y are not part of the standard alphabet of Italian by comparing the Italian and English alphabets to find the missing letters

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing that days of the week and months of the year are written with lower-case letters by reading a short text such as the poems ‘Filastrocca della settimana’ (‘Tanto sole il lunedì’) and ‘Trenta giorni ha novembre’, and searching for examples

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning the structure of simple statements and questions based on models, for example, lo sono Anna. Non sto bene.; È un gatto? Sì, è un gatto.

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning simple verbs to describe actions and using them in formulaic expressions (e.g. Guardo la televisione; Ascolto la musica; Leggo il librol), for example, creating a gesture to match the verb, and playing Simon says with the verbs and their matching gestures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how likes and dislikes are expressed in Italian (e.g. Ti piace la pizza?; Mi piace l’ananas; Non mi piace il formaggio), for example, by selecting cards for each statement for the pizza toppings that they like and dislike, asking other students, and reporting to the class

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing negation using non (e.g. Non sono bassa; Non ho un cane) by playing a circle game in which they have to change places with someone else who shares the same answer

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that adjectives are used to describe people, objects or places and are usually placed after the noun (e.g. la penna rossa), for example, making a picture sequence of items with different colours with a description below, and drawing a box around the adjective

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using pronouns to identify people (e.g. io, tu, lui, lei, noi, voi, loro), playing a pronoun race, where images of well-known characters from books, television or movies are displayed on the board with their English pronouns, and students race to correctly match the corresponding Italian pronoun in the fastest time

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the formulaic use of the verbs essere and avere to give personal information about state or identity (e.g. Ho due fratelli; Sono basso; Ho 6 anni; Ho gli occhi verdi; Sono alto), by creating a class chart of essere and avere with images underneath to match the verbs

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2U04 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: identify that written and spoken Italian has grammatical structures and other language features that may be similar to or different from English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying cognates and loan words (words that share a similar spelling, meaning and pronunciation), comparing similarities and differences between Italian and English (e.g. banana, computer, università, animale, appartamento), and creating a class poster

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing English words that are the same in Italian (e.g. weekend, sport), and Italian words that are the same in English (e.g. pizza, piano, lava), for example, by making a pair of ‘Invaders in English’ and ‘Invaders in Italian’ posters, and adding words on sticky notes as they arise

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing gender in patterns of naming, for example, comparing the names Paolo/Paola and Alessandro/Alessandra, and noticing that Italian words for people, places and things (called ‘nouns’) have a gender, and that gender is indicated in most cases with an a or o at the end of the word, for example, by making an ‘I wonder’ chart to categorise nouns with different endings

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that some Italian nouns in the singular end in an e, and having dictionary races to find out what their gender is

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Italian forms the singular and plural differently from English, and noticing that the ending of Italian nouns change when there is more than one (called ‘plural’), and that a becomes e, o becomes i, and e becomes i, for example, by playing Ciuf! Ciuf! (make the train), where two teams sit in two columns and students have to respond correctly to the flashcard to stand and become a carriage, and the winning team calls Ciuf! Ciuf!

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that Italian has many words for ‘the’ (called ‘definite articles’), and that these words match the gender of the nouns, for example, by playing matching games such as ‘memory’ or ‘go fish’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that in Italian the definite article l’ is used when the noun starts with a vowel, and lo when the noun starts with a z, and playing circle games where each article has a different gesture (e.g. la = 2 taps on head, il = 2 taps on shoulders, l’ = 2 taps on knees, lo = 2 claps)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that the definite articles change when there is more than one noun, becoming le, i and gli, for example, by spotting them in a song video such as ‘Le ruote del bus’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that Italian has definite and indefinite articles that are gender based, for example, la casa, una casa; il giardino, un giardino; lo zoo, uno zoo

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that some words for asking questions are similar to English and do not change (e.g. Chi?; Cosa?; Quando?), whereas others change to denote number and gender (e.g. Quanto/Quanti?)

as_extracts.name: LITAF102-E09
as_extracts.description: They start to develop written competence by copying letters and words, and then produce the language with support.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2C05 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using words, familiar phrases and modelled language

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and reproducing in written form the sounds of the Italian language, for example, tracing the vowels and imitating the sound in simple word parts, such as ba, be, bi, bo and bu

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating words from known vowels, consonants and clusters, for example, by arranging laminated or magnetic letters to form target vocabulary or phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising vocabulary sets by creating their own flashcards, wordlists, labelled diagrams, recipes, signage or manifesto da ricercato (‘Wanted’ poster)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: labelling sequenced pictures, with support, to describe events or recreate a fairytale

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing aspects of their personal world by drawing and writing captions such as Ecco il mio papà / mio fratello, for example, creating a real or imaginary family tree; or illustrating a ‘Big Book’ with the class and presenting it with gestures, miming the story, for example, È un uccello. È verde. L’uccello vola. La farfalla è gialla. La rana è verde. La zebra è bianca e nera.

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing feelings about a book/video clip in simple ‘reviews’ by writing their names under one of the following statements: Mi piace; Mi piace molto; Non mi piace

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing from words, phrases and sentences provided to express ideas to match a visual or aural prompt, for example, È Marco; È grande; È bravo

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering simple questions (e.g. Come ti chiami?; Come stai?; Quanti anni hai?) with short formulaic responses, for example, by interviewing members of the class to create a personal profile or survey

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing people in a photo by naming family members and friends (e.g. mio fratello Carlo; la mia amica del cuore, Gina), using flashcards, wordlists, posters, photos and multimedia slides as support

as_extracts.name: LITAF102-E10
as_extracts.description: They respond to texts using frequently used words, phrases and sentence patterns in both written and spoken language.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2C01 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: communicate using formulaic and modelled language relating to aspects of their personal world

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that the teacher uses the informal form with students and students use the formal form with the teacher, for example, using Buongiorno or Presente for the roll call, not Ciao

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that there are greetings for different times of the day (e.g. Buongiorno; Buon pomeriggio; Buonasera; Buonanotte), and it is not uncommon to hear Buonasera in the early afternoon, after a nap, or at the end of the school day, for example, playing charades with activities to guess the time of day and the greeting

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: introducing themselves and answering questions, for example, Come ti chiami? Mi chiamo …, e tu?; Quanti anni hai? Ho cinque anni, e tu?; Come stai? Bene, e tu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing people and belongings, using familiar formulaic expressions, for example, Questo/a è …; Ecco il mio pallone; Ecco un gelato al limone; Buonissimo!

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing information about simple everyday actions in the present tense, for example, Gioco a football; Mangio la pizza; Leggo il libro

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing likes and dislikes, for example, Sì, mi piace; No, non mi piace

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using set phrases to indicate possession (e.g. la mia penna; il mio cane; il mio papà; la mia mamma), and then playing the stealing game by passing soft toys around the classroom and using target language to claim ownership of an item to ‘steal’ it, for example, il mio cane

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using formulaic Italian phrases for everyday interactions such as thanking, apologising and offering congratulations, for example, Grazie mille! Prego; Mi dispiace; Auguri!

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing images of a variety of family and pet pictures (their own and others’), and describing them using simple structures, for example, È la mia mamma. La mia mamma è alta; È il cane. È carino.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2C02 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: participate in a range of guided language activities using formulaic expressions, and visual and spoken cues

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: pointing to objects named in Italian

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to guided collective activities such as illustrating and labelling a poster

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: working in pairs or groups to select given options relating to foods, toys or classroom items, for example, Vuoi / Cosa vuoi? Voglio una pesca.; Posso avere …?; E tu, cosa prendi?; Ti piace l’orsacchiotto?; Ecco la penna blu.

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using formulaic phrases to show politeness (e.g. Grazie! Prego; Scusa; Per favore; Bene; Molto bene; Buon appetito!) by doing a role-play, for example, eating in a restaurant

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a guided role-play in a shop or at the market, for example, Una banana per favore. Ecco. Quanto costa?; Un gelato per favore. Ecco il gelato.

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a show-and-tell, for example, Questa è la mia bambola. Si chiama Teresa.; Questo è il mio camion. È grande.

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reciting and performing chants, rhymes and songs, and adding music and actions to support meaning in their own performances, for example, the ‘Farfallina’ rhyme: Farfallina bella bianca, vola vola e mai si stanca. Vola vola sempre in su, farfallina non c’è più, resti fuori solo tu!

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using props such as emoji faces to practise Sto bene, Sto male and Così così

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that formal greetings are used with adults other than friends or family (e.g. Buongiorno; Salve; ArrivederLa) and informal greetings (e.g. Ciao; Salve) are used with family and friends, for example, by acting out short role-plays to demonstrate their use, and creating dos and don’ts posters for the classroom

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2C03 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: locate key information in a variety of texts with support, and respond using gestures, images, words and/or formulaic phrases
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying target words in stories and videos, and then identifying the main idea or an event by brainstorming words related to an image, such as la festa, la scuola, lo zoo, la spiaggia and l’estate, and retelling the event using these words

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: miming, drawing, and onscreen pointing, clicking or dragging to show their understanding of key points in a range of texts such as a picture book, song, poem, video clip, rhyme or cartoon strip

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sequencing pictures and simple text in the order that events occurred, and then retelling a story or information by creating a storyboard, using speech bubbles to show direct speech

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising phrases from classroom routines, images and labels, such as days of the week, subjects, rules, labels, weather, seasons and dates, and creating word posters for the classroom

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to games or songs with actions or miming, for example, the song ‘Testa, spalle, ginocchia e piedi’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying words in a variety of texts, for example, by annotating a written text with images to match the words, or by listening for keywords in a spoken text and holding up a matching card for each word they hear

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and recreating common Italian gestures, facial expressions and intonation patterns that express likes, dislikes and feelings (e.g. for Eccellente!; Squisito!; Non lo so), for example, by viewing short video reels or commercials and ticking them off a list when they appear

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing formalities in Italy such as handshakes or standing up to greet a visitor to the classroom, and using simple gestures to add emphasis to expressions, for example, joining their thumb and index finger to form an O, meaning ‘thumbs up’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring common exclamations and interjections (e.g. Boh!; Mamma mia!; Salute!; Bravo!; Allora …) by viewing video clips, commercials and short reels, and creating role-plays with partners or puppets to demonstrate situations where they are suitable

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and making meaning of words and phrases through fairytales and stories, for example, by reading or viewing the ‘Cappuccetto Rosso’ fairytale, singing the song ‘Mi piace Cappuccetto Rosso’ to practise expressing likes and dislikes, or performing it as a short play using the characters to experience and practise live interactive language

È verde. L’uccello vola. La farfalla è gialla. La rana è verde. La zebra è bianca e nera.

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing feelings about a book/video clip in simple ‘reviews’ by writing their names under one of the following statements: Mi piace; Mi piace molto; Non mi piace

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing from words, phrases and sentences provided to express ideas to match a visual or aural prompt, for example, È Marco; È grande; È bravo

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering simple questions (e.g. Come ti chiami?; Come stai?; Quanti anni hai?) with short formulaic responses, for example, by interviewing members of the class to create a personal profile or survey

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing people in a photo by naming family members and friends (e.g. mio fratello Carlo; la mia amica del cuore, Gina), using flashcards, wordlists, posters, photos and multimedia slides as support

as_extracts.name: LITAF102-E13
as_extracts.description: Students explore and recognise the influence of culture on language and identity.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2E04 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: explore connections between language and culture through play and/or imagination
content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with Italian Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating Italy on a world map, understanding that Italian is the national language of Italy and that it is spoken in Italian-speaking communities around the world, and highlighting relevant countries and regions on the map

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: making connections with Italian words and phrases used in everyday life in Australia, for example, identifying food names such as spaghetti, pasta, cappuccino and latte

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that there are loan words in English from Italian (e.g. gelato, pizza), as well as many loan words in Italian from English (e.g. lo sport) and other languages (e.g. il bazar from Persian)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing, through a range of resources (e.g. photos and video clips) that members of Italian-speaking communities may do everyday things differently from themselves (e.g. shaking hands, kissing on the cheek and starting a meal with Buon appetito!), and then doing a role-play, for example, going to a restaurant with a friend

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a shared reading of ‘La Befana’ story and singing the song ‘La Befana viene di notte’; exploring il Carnevale through the ‘Carnevale’ song and making masks or coriandoli pictures; creating la Festa dei Nonni cards; listening to ‘L’inno di Mameli’ for la Festa della Repubblica; and having a Ferragosto picnic

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging ideas, feelings and understandings of language and culture through play-based experiences, for example, dress-ups; playing pretend cafe, pizzeria and market stands; playing with puppets

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that music, dance, food, celebrations and games are connected with culture, such as eating panettone at Christmas and playing il gioco del Truc at Easter, and play-acting a celebration using the appropriate gestures and language

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in actions, movement or dance, such as la tarantella

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with cultural items such as Euros, postcards and authentic resources from Italy, and using them as a prompt to create imaginary stories

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing simple Italian games such as bocce, clapping games (e.g. batti le manine), and circle games (e.g. il contadino nel prato)

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2U05 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: reflect on how language, culture and identity are interconnected and discuss how Italian-speaking communities are similar to or different from others
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U05-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing images of daily life in Italy and Australia, and noticing and comparing similarities and differences in, for example, l’autobus, il mercato, il supermercato or la fontana

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U05-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the range of languages and cultures in their classroom, and creating a collage using pictures and photos of cultural celebrations and events and formulaic expressions associated with them, for example, Ferragosto and la Befana (la festa del 6 gennaio)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U05-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: taking an evening walk with family at home and recognising that the Italian tradition of fare la passeggiata is culturally more significant than just taking a walk

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U05-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that music, dance, food, celebrations and games are connected with culture, for example, exploring la Festa delle Castagne (where people gather at the marketplace in late autumn to eat roasted chestnuts and listen to traditional music) by viewing online videos and roasting chestnuts in an air fryer

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U05-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing language associated with interactions such as the use of first names in Australian or US English compared with the use of titles and family names in Italian, for example, Professor/Professoressa with a teacher and Signor/Signora with an adult, and then taking on a character and referring to each other with the correct title for the rest of the class

as_extracts.name: LITAF102-E14
as_extracts.description: They recognise that Italian is spoken in communities and regions in Australia and around the world, and relate this to their own language(s) and culture(s).

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2U06 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: identify where Italian is used around the world and recognise that there are many different languages spoken in communities throughout Australia
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U06-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching the countries where different languages are spoken and discussing why the world has many different languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U06-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that many languages from different parts of the world are spoken in Australia and may be represented in their classroom, and creating a speech bubble that introduces them and the language(s) they speak

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U06-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and celebrating that Australian communities are made up of many different languages and cultures, for example, by observing International Mother Language Day on 21 February and coming to class in the traditional clothing of their choice

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U06-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how local names of streets, places and landmarks can have their origins in language(s) of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, identifying the meanings of these place names, for example, ‘You Yangs’ comes from the Wadawurrung words Wurdi Youang, meaning ‘big hill’, and then discussing the names of Italian landforms that also denote physical characteristics, such as Monte Bianco

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U06-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching symbols and colours used by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and by Italian-speaking communities in a range of contexts, for example, identifying the colours on a range of flags from different countries and communities in Italian and discussing what the colours represent in English

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U06-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that languages and communities have different protocols regarding the use of terms of respect, for example, there are ways of addressing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples using familial terms (e.g. ‘Uncle’ or ‘Aunty’), depending on the relationship, and comparing these terms with Italian and/or other languages

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

curriculum_content_description.strand_title: Engaging with Italian Language and Culture
curriculum_content_description.strand_tag: Engaging with Italian Language and Culture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2E01 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: notice that Italian looks and sounds different to other languages
substrand_content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with Italian Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E01-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to Italian and English words, and noticing features of spoken Italian that help them to identify the Italian words, such as pronunciation and frequently repeated sounds, for example, by listening to and comparing nursery rhymes, counting songs and chants, such as ‘Le ruote del bus’, ‘Brilla, brilla la stellina’ and ‘Se sei felice e tu lo sai’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E01-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that most words in Standard Italian end with the vowels a, e, i, o and u, and making 5 gestures for them: swinging arm for e for ‘elephant’, cupped hand for i for ‘igloo’, wiggling finger for o for ‘octopus’, Auslan sign for a for ‘ask’ and pushing gesture for u for ‘push’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E01-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing that written Italian uses the same letters as written English, and noticing that Italian has 21 letters, English has 26 and some Italian letters have accent marks

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E01-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with animal sounds in Italian, for example, comparing the sounds bau bau (dog), pio pio (chick) and hiii (horse) with those in English and in other languages spoken by class members

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E01-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording students creating single Italian words or sounds using digital recording software, and then playing the audio back and listening for aspects of pronunciation that are unique to Italian

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E01-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing that some words that do not end with a vowel are the same in Italian and English, such as computer, robot, yoghurt and sport, and discussing the reasons why they may be the same

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E01-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing gender in patterns of naming, for example, comparing the names Paolo/Paola and Alessandro/Alessandra

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2E02 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: develop oral language skills through exploring and listening to the sounds and patterns of the language
substrand_content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with Italian Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E02-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in songs, chants and rhymes to imitate Italian pronunciation, intonation and stress, for example, ‘Ciao buongiorno’; ‘Tanti auguri a te’; ‘Giro girotondo’; ‘Cinque scimmiette saltavano sul letto’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E02-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with new sets of vocabulary by moving about the classroom to touch and identify items such as objects, flashcards, images and toys, and expanding vocabulary by naming soft-toy animals

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E02-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing vocabulary by playing games such as ‘odd one out’ (where 4 words are said or pictured, and students must identify the incorrect one), ‘6 corners’ (where students go to one of 6 numbered points around the room where a vocabulary word is written, and then when the dice is rolled those of that number sit on the floor), and find your match (where Italian/English or Italian/image card pairs are distributed to the students and they have to find their partner)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E02-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using digital interactive resources to practise sequencing and ordering

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E02-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using call-and-response games, songs and chants to consolidate language patterns

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E02-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing circle games such as ‘buzz’ with numbers or vowel sounds, Ho fatto la spesa e comprato …; Cane, cane chi ha l’osso?, or ‘broken telephone’, where a vocabulary word is whispered along a line of 5 and the last person reveals the word

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E02-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: building memory skills and reinforcing vocabulary acquisition by playing games, for example, Salta se hai …; Simone dice …; Io spio …

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E02-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing their own use of words, expressions or behaviours that make them who they are, including words from different languages and ways of celebrating or talking that may not be familiar to other people

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E02-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the different languages spoken by members of the class and listening to the different sounds and ways of saying common expressions such as ‘Good morning’ or ‘Hello’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E02-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing personal name traditions in the languages spoken by members of the class

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2E03 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and respond to greetings, instructions and language relating to their personal world using one- or 2-word responses and/or single-idea phrases
substrand_content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with Italian Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E03-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using Italian for everyday routines such as roll call or opening and closing lessons, for example, singing ‘Ciao, buongiorno’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E03-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to teacher instructions (e.g. In piedi!; Seduti!; In cerchio!; Insieme, qui!; Attenzione!; Non parlare!; Silenzio!; Alza la mano!)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E03-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using single words for personal actions such as scrivo, taglio, incollo and coloro to play a game, for example, miming a gesture or action to elicit the target word

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E03-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple greetings relevant to the time of day, the celebration or event, and their relationship to the listener, such as Ciao, Salve, Buongiorno, Arrivederci, Tanti auguri, Buona Pasqua and Buon Natale

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E03-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: making classroom requests such as Posso andare in bagno? and Posso andare a bere?

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E03-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing charades for feeling words, using appropriate gestures, facial expressions and body language

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E03-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing a picture of their real or fictional family, naming family members and friends, for example, mio fratello Carlo; il papà Tom

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E03-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing likes and dislikes (e.g. Sì; No; Mi piace; Non mi piace), and practising responses by playing games such as ‘secret sugar glider’, where posters of characters with 5 likes and dislikes are posted around the room, each student is secretly given a card with a character, and students ask each other questions about their 5 likes and dislikes (Ti piace …?) to find out which character they match with

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E03-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to the roll call by giving simple personal details in response to a prompt, for example, Ho sette anni

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E03-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to games or songs with actions or miming, for example, participating in call-and-response games (e.g. Faccio la pizza) or songs (e.g. ‘Testa, spalla, ginocchia e piedi’)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2E04 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: explore connections between language and culture through play and/or imagination
substrand_content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with Italian Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating Italy on a world map, understanding that Italian is the national language of Italy and that it is spoken in Italian-speaking communities around the world, and highlighting relevant countries and regions on the map

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: making connections with Italian words and phrases used in everyday life in Australia, for example, identifying food names such as spaghetti, pasta, cappuccino and latte

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that there are loan words in English from Italian (e.g. gelato, pizza), as well as many loan words in Italian from English (e.g. lo sport) and other languages (e.g. il bazar from Persian)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing, through a range of resources (e.g. photos and video clips) that members of Italian-speaking communities may do everyday things differently from themselves (e.g. shaking hands, kissing on the cheek and starting a meal with Buon appetito!), and then doing a role-play, for example, going to a restaurant with a friend

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a shared reading of ‘La Befana’ story and singing the song ‘La Befana viene di notte’; exploring il Carnevale through the ‘Carnevale’ song and making masks or coriandoli pictures; creating la Festa dei Nonni cards; listening to ‘L’inno di Mameli’ for la Festa della Repubblica; and having a Ferragosto picnic

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging ideas, feelings and understandings of language and culture through play-based experiences, for example, dress-ups; playing pretend cafe, pizzeria and market stands; playing with puppets

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that music, dance, food, celebrations and games are connected with culture, such as eating panettone at Christmas and playing il gioco del Truc at Easter, and play-acting a celebration using the appropriate gestures and language

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in actions, movement or dance, such as la tarantella

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with cultural items such as Euros, postcards and authentic resources from Italy, and using them as a prompt to create imaginary stories

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2E04-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing simple Italian games such as bocce, clapping games (e.g. batti le manine), and circle games (e.g. il contadino nel prato)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2C01 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: communicate using formulaic and modelled language relating to aspects of their personal world

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that the teacher uses the informal form with students and students use the formal form with the teacher, for example, using Buongiorno or Presente for the roll call, not Ciao

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that there are greetings for different times of the day (e.g. Buongiorno; Buon pomeriggio; Buonasera; Buonanotte), and it is not uncommon to hear Buonasera in the early afternoon, after a nap, or at the end of the school day, for example, playing charades with activities to guess the time of day and the greeting

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: introducing themselves and answering questions, for example, Come ti chiami? Mi chiamo …, e tu?; Quanti anni hai? Ho cinque anni, e tu?; Come stai? Bene, e tu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing people and belongings, using familiar formulaic expressions, for example, Questo/a è …; Ecco il mio pallone; Ecco un gelato al limone; Buonissimo!

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing information about simple everyday actions in the present tense, for example, Gioco a football; Mangio la pizza; Leggo il libro

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing likes and dislikes, for example, Sì, mi piace; No, non mi piace

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using set phrases to indicate possession (e.g. la mia penna; il mio cane; il mio papà; la mia mamma), and then playing the stealing game by passing soft toys around the classroom and using target language to claim ownership of an item to ‘steal’ it, for example, il mio cane

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using formulaic Italian phrases for everyday interactions such as thanking, apologising and offering congratulations, for example, Grazie mille! Prego; Mi dispiace; Auguri!

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C01-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing images of a variety of family and pet pictures (their own and others’), and describing them using simple structures, for example, È la mia mamma. La mia mamma è alta; È il cane. È carino.

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2C02 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in a range of guided language activities using formulaic expressions, and visual and spoken cues

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: pointing to objects named in Italian

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to guided collective activities such as illustrating and labelling a poster

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: working in pairs or groups to select given options relating to foods, toys or classroom items, for example, Vuoi / Cosa vuoi? Voglio una pesca.; Posso avere …?; E tu, cosa prendi?; Ti piace l’orsacchiotto?; Ecco la penna blu.

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using formulaic phrases to show politeness (e.g. Grazie! Prego; Scusa; Per favore; Bene; Molto bene; Buon appetito!) by doing a role-play, for example, eating in a restaurant

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a guided role-play in a shop or at the market, for example, Una banana per favore. Ecco. Quanto costa?; Un gelato per favore. Ecco il gelato.

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a show-and-tell, for example, Questa è la mia bambola. Si chiama Teresa.; Questo è il mio camion. È grande.

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reciting and performing chants, rhymes and songs, and adding music and actions to support meaning in their own performances, for example, the ‘Farfallina’ rhyme: Farfallina bella bianca, vola vola e mai si stanca. Vola vola sempre in su, farfallina non c’è più, resti fuori solo tu!

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using props such as emoji faces to practise Sto bene, Sto male and Così così

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C02-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that formal greetings are used with adults other than friends or family (e.g. Buongiorno; Salve; ArrivederLa) and informal greetings (e.g. Ciao; Salve) are used with family and friends, for example, by acting out short role-plays to demonstrate their use, and creating dos and don’ts posters for the classroom

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Mediating meaning in and between languages
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2C03 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate key information in a variety of texts with support, and respond using gestures, images, words and/or formulaic phrases
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying target words in stories and videos, and then identifying the main idea or an event by brainstorming words related to an image, such as la festa, la scuola, lo zoo, la spiaggia and l’estate, and retelling the event using these words

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: miming, drawing, and onscreen pointing, clicking or dragging to show their understanding of key points in a range of texts such as a picture book, song, poem, video clip, rhyme or cartoon strip

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sequencing pictures and simple text in the order that events occurred, and then retelling a story or information by creating a storyboard, using speech bubbles to show direct speech

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising phrases from classroom routines, images and labels, such as days of the week, subjects, rules, labels, weather, seasons and dates, and creating word posters for the classroom

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to games or songs with actions or miming, for example, the song ‘Testa, spalle, ginocchia e piedi’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying words in a variety of texts, for example, by annotating a written text with images to match the words, or by listening for keywords in a spoken text and holding up a matching card for each word they hear

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and recreating common Italian gestures, facial expressions and intonation patterns that express likes, dislikes and feelings (e.g. for Eccellente!; Squisito!; Non lo so), for example, by viewing short video reels or commercials and ticking them off a list when they appear

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing formalities in Italy such as handshakes or standing up to greet a visitor to the classroom, and using simple gestures to add emphasis to expressions, for example, joining their thumb and index finger to form an O, meaning ‘thumbs up’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring common exclamations and interjections (e.g. Boh!; Mamma mia!; Salute!; Bravo!; Allora …) by viewing video clips, commercials and short reels, and creating role-plays with partners or puppets to demonstrate situations where they are suitable

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C03-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and making meaning of words and phrases through fairytales and stories, for example, by reading or viewing the ‘Cappuccetto Rosso’ fairytale, singing the song ‘Mi piace Cappuccetto Rosso’ to practise expressing likes and dislikes, or performing it as a short play using the characters to experience and practise live interactive language

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2C04 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: explore and make meaning from sounds, words and phrases for familiar objects or terms in Italian through play, and discover how languages influence each other
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C04-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in songs that may include actions, movement or dance, for example, ‘Mi piace Cappuccetto Rosso’; ‘Testa, spalle, ginocchia, piedi’; ‘Giro girotondo’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C04-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing games, for example, counting games, sorting and order games, retrieving games to demonstrate possession, number games or traditional Italian games such as tombola, ruba bandiera and bocce

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C04-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging ideas, feelings and understandings of language and/or culture through play-based experiences, for example, dress-ups; playing pretend cafe, pizzeria and market stands; and playing with puppets

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C04-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying familiar objects in the classroom by labelling, naming, pointing, matching, clicking and dragging, and drawing and tracing letters

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2C05 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using words, familiar phrases and modelled language

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and reproducing in written form the sounds of the Italian language, for example, tracing the vowels and imitating the sound in simple word parts, such as ba, be, bi, bo and bu

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating words from known vowels, consonants and clusters, for example, by arranging laminated or magnetic letters to form target vocabulary or phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising vocabulary sets by creating their own flashcards, wordlists, labelled diagrams, recipes, signage or manifesto da ricercato (‘Wanted’ poster)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: labelling sequenced pictures, with support, to describe events or recreate a fairytale

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing aspects of their personal world by drawing and writing captions such as Ecco il mio papà / mio fratello, for example, creating a real or imaginary family tree; or illustrating a ‘Big Book’ with the class and presenting it with gestures, miming the story, for example, È un uccello. È verde. L’uccello vola. La farfalla è gialla. La rana è verde. La zebra è bianca e nera.

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing feelings about a book/video clip in simple ‘reviews’ by writing their names under one of the following statements: Mi piace; Mi piace molto; Non mi piace

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing from words, phrases and sentences provided to express ideas to match a visual or aural prompt, for example, È Marco; È grande; È bravo

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering simple questions (e.g. Come ti chiami?; Come stai?; Quanti anni hai?) with short formulaic responses, for example, by interviewing members of the class to create a personal profile or survey

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2C05-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing people in a photo by naming family members and friends (e.g. mio fratello Carlo; la mia amica del cuore, Gina), using flashcards, wordlists, posters, photos and multimedia slides as support

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2U01 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: imitate the pronunciation and intonation of spoken Italian, and understand how sounds are produced

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U01-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to the language in a short video clip with Italian subtitles, and noticing that Italian is a phonetic language that sounds generally as it is written

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U01-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing vowel sounds in Italian and English, for example, making up nonsense words and trying to spell them to conform with Italian phonetics, for example, playing spot the odd one out from strings of words (e.g. casa, rana, muffa, papa)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U01-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reproducing Italian sounds and intonation patterns through imitation, such as reciting nursery rhymes or tongue twisters and singing songs, such as ‘La canzone dell’alfabeto’, the AEIOU song and ‘Il gatto fa miao’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U01-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using Italian patterns of intonation, pronunciation and stress, for example, by playing rhyming tennis, where partners say vowels back and forth to each other in nonsense words, changing the consonant when they get back to a (e.g. lala, lele, lili, lolo, lulu, mama, meme, mimi, momo, mumu)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U01-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing that words which stress the final letter have an accent on that letter (e.g. papà, città), for example, finding examples in a simple text such as a nursery rhyme or poem (e.g. ‘La casetta delle vocali’)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U01-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing syllable patterns in words such as la-sa-gna and pa-ta-ta and clapping out the syllables

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U01-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that questions are denoted by rising intonation, not the sentence structure

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U01-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that different dialects are spoken in Italy and accents vary in Italian-speaking communities by listening to or viewing audio and visual texts from a range of regions in Italy

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2U02 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify sound combinations to produce simple words, and then an increasing number of frequently used words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U02-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising rolling their rs by reciting rhymes and chants

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U02-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that the letter c as in ciao sounds like ‘ch’ in English and that the letters ch as in chi sounds like a ‘k’ in English, and making a list of ‘tricky letters’ with pronunciation hints

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U02-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that there are spelling rules in Italian that affect pronunciation, such as ci, ce, gi and ge

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U02-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing a dictionary game to collect as many words as possible relating to a topic provided by the teacher in a set amount of time

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2U03 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and explore how the Roman alphabet and features of language are used to construct meaning in Italian

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating the pronunciation of the 21 letters of the Italian alphabet by singing along with the online video of the Italian alphabet song

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that the letters j, k, w, x and y are not part of the standard alphabet of Italian by comparing the Italian and English alphabets to find the missing letters

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing that days of the week and months of the year are written with lower-case letters by reading a short text such as the poems ‘Filastrocca della settimana’ (‘Tanto sole il lunedì’) and ‘Trenta giorni ha novembre’, and searching for examples

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning the structure of simple statements and questions based on models, for example, lo sono Anna. Non sto bene.; È un gatto? Sì, è un gatto.

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning simple verbs to describe actions and using them in formulaic expressions (e.g. Guardo la televisione; Ascolto la musica; Leggo il librol), for example, creating a gesture to match the verb, and playing Simon says with the verbs and their matching gestures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how likes and dislikes are expressed in Italian (e.g. Ti piace la pizza?; Mi piace l’ananas; Non mi piace il formaggio), for example, by selecting cards for each statement for the pizza toppings that they like and dislike, asking other students, and reporting to the class

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing negation using non (e.g. Non sono bassa; Non ho un cane) by playing a circle game in which they have to change places with someone else who shares the same answer

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that adjectives are used to describe people, objects or places and are usually placed after the noun (e.g. la penna rossa), for example, making a picture sequence of items with different colours with a description below, and drawing a box around the adjective

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using pronouns to identify people (e.g. io, tu, lui, lei, noi, voi, loro), playing a pronoun race, where images of well-known characters from books, television or movies are displayed on the board with their English pronouns, and students race to correctly match the corresponding Italian pronoun in the fastest time

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U03-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the formulaic use of the verbs essere and avere to give personal information about state or identity (e.g. Ho due fratelli; Sono basso; Ho 6 anni; Ho gli occhi verdi; Sono alto), by creating a class chart of essere and avere with images underneath to match the verbs

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2U04 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify that written and spoken Italian has grammatical structures and other language features that may be similar to or different from English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying cognates and loan words (words that share a similar spelling, meaning and pronunciation), comparing similarities and differences between Italian and English (e.g. banana, computer, università, animale, appartamento), and creating a class poster

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing English words that are the same in Italian (e.g. weekend, sport), and Italian words that are the same in English (e.g. pizza, piano, lava), for example, by making a pair of ‘Invaders in English’ and ‘Invaders in Italian’ posters, and adding words on sticky notes as they arise

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing gender in patterns of naming, for example, comparing the names Paolo/Paola and Alessandro/Alessandra, and noticing that Italian words for people, places and things (called ‘nouns’) have a gender, and that gender is indicated in most cases with an a or o at the end of the word, for example, by making an ‘I wonder’ chart to categorise nouns with different endings

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that some Italian nouns in the singular end in an e, and having dictionary races to find out what their gender is

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Italian forms the singular and plural differently from English, and noticing that the ending of Italian nouns change when there is more than one (called ‘plural’), and that a becomes e, o becomes i, and e becomes i, for example, by playing Ciuf! Ciuf! (make the train), where two teams sit in two columns and students have to respond correctly to the flashcard to stand and become a carriage, and the winning team calls Ciuf! Ciuf!

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that Italian has many words for ‘the’ (called ‘definite articles’), and that these words match the gender of the nouns, for example, by playing matching games such as ‘memory’ or ‘go fish’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that in Italian the definite article l’ is used when the noun starts with a vowel, and lo when the noun starts with a z, and playing circle games where each article has a different gesture (e.g. la = 2 taps on head, il = 2 taps on shoulders, l’ = 2 taps on knees, lo = 2 claps)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that the definite articles change when there is more than one noun, becoming le, i and gli, for example, by spotting them in a song video such as ‘Le ruote del bus’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that Italian has definite and indefinite articles that are gender based, for example, la casa, una casa; il giardino, un giardino; lo zoo, uno zoo

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U04-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that some words for asking questions are similar to English and do not change (e.g. Chi?; Cosa?; Quando?), whereas others change to denote number and gender (e.g. Quanto/Quanti?)

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2U05 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: reflect on how language, culture and identity are interconnected and discuss how Italian-speaking communities are similar to or different from others
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U05-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing images of daily life in Italy and Australia, and noticing and comparing similarities and differences in, for example, l’autobus, il mercato, il supermercato or la fontana

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U05-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the range of languages and cultures in their classroom, and creating a collage using pictures and photos of cultural celebrations and events and formulaic expressions associated with them, for example, Ferragosto and la Befana (la festa del 6 gennaio)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U05-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: taking an evening walk with family at home and recognising that the Italian tradition of fare la passeggiata is culturally more significant than just taking a walk

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U05-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that music, dance, food, celebrations and games are connected with culture, for example, exploring la Festa delle Castagne (where people gather at the marketplace in late autumn to eat roasted chestnuts and listen to traditional music) by viewing online videos and roasting chestnuts in an air fryer

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U05-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing language associated with interactions such as the use of first names in Australian or US English compared with the use of titles and family names in Italian, for example, Professor/Professoressa with a teacher and Signor/Signora with an adult, and then taking on a character and referring to each other with the correct title for the rest of the class

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT2U06 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify where Italian is used around the world and recognise that there are many different languages spoken in communities throughout Australia
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U06-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching the countries where different languages are spoken and discussing why the world has many different languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U06-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that many languages from different parts of the world are spoken in Australia and may be represented in their classroom, and creating a speech bubble that introduces them and the language(s) they speak

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U06-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and celebrating that Australian communities are made up of many different languages and cultures, for example, by observing International Mother Language Day on 21 February and coming to class in the traditional clothing of their choice

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U06-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how local names of streets, places and landmarks can have their origins in language(s) of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, identifying the meanings of these place names, for example, ‘You Yangs’ comes from the Wadawurrung words Wurdi Youang, meaning ‘big hill’, and then discussing the names of Italian landforms that also denote physical characteristics, such as Monte Bianco

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U06-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching symbols and colours used by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and by Italian-speaking communities in a range of contexts, for example, identifying the colours on a range of flags from different countries and communities in Italian and discussing what the colours represent in English

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT2U06-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that languages and communities have different protocols regarding the use of terms of respect, for example, there are ways of addressing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples using familial terms (e.g. ‘Uncle’ or ‘Aunty’), depending on the relationship, and comparing these terms with Italian and/or other languages

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 3 and 4, Italian language learning builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences with language. Students communicate and work in collaboration with their peers and teachers through purposeful and creative play in structured activities that involve listening, speaking, reading, writing and viewing. They use Italian to interact with their peers and teachers and to participate in activities in familiar settings that reflect their interests and capabilities. They use local and digital resources to explore Italian-speaking communities. They continue to receive extensive support through modelling, scaffolding and repetition, as well as the use of targeted resources.

Students develop active listening skills and use gestures, words and modelled expressions, imitating the sounds, pronunciation and intonation of Italian. They locate information, and respond to and create texts using written and spoken Italian. They access authentic and purpose-developed Italian-language texts such as picture books, stories, songs, digital and animated games, timetables, recipes and advertisements. They recognise the interconnected nature of language, culture and identity.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 4, students use Italian to initiate structured interactions and share information related to the classroom and their personal worlds. They use modelled language to participate in spoken and written activities. They locate and respond to key items of information in texts, using strategies to help interpret and convey meaning in familiar contexts. They use modelled language and basic grammatical structures to create texts.

Students imitate the sound combinations and rhythms of spoken Italian. They demonstrate their understanding that Italian has non-verbal, spoken and written language conventions and rules to convey meaning. They recognise that some terms have cultural meanings. They identify patterns in Italian and make comparisons between Italian and English, using simple metalanguage. They understand how aspects of language and culture contribute to their own and others’ identity.

as_extracts.name: LITAF104-E01
as_extracts.description: students use Italian to initiate structured interactions and share information related to the classroom and their personal worlds.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT4C01 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: initiate exchanges and respond to modelled questions about themselves, others and the classroom environment, using formulaic expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C01-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging personal information and responding to questions about themselves, their family, leisure activities, neighbourhood and daily experiences, and food, for example, Da dove vieni? Da Torino; Sono italiano, e tu?; Chi sei? Sono …, e tu?; Chi è …? Lui/lei è …; … è mio padre; Questo/a è …, e questo/a?; È mio fratello; Dove abiti? Abito in via … / a …, e tu?

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C01-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in classroom activities by asking for clarification, permission, help or repetition, praising and complimenting, for example, Come si dice …?; Non ho capito. Può ripetere?; Posso prendere/fare/avere qualcosa? Sì/no. Non è possibile / Non adesso; Come?; Aiuto, per favore

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C01-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging simple spoken or written messages to praise or compliment someone, for example, Bravo/a!; Ottimo!; È bello / molto bello

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C01-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing themselves, their friends and objects with the correct placement of adjectives, for example, La camicia è rossa/nuova/piccola; Sono biondo/alto/grasso; … è bruno/giovane; Il nonno ha i capelli castani; Ha gli occhi molto grandi; … ha i capelli / gli occhi / il naso / la bocca + adjective

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C01-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to a partner’s questions, for example, Di che colore è la maglia? È rosa; Qual è il tuo/suo gioco preferito?

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C01-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing location using prepositions of place, for example, for objects in the home, such as Il vaso è sopra il tavolo; L’albero è a sinistra; L’auto è dentro il garage

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C01-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing routines, for example, ieri/oggi/domani/ora/dopo; Che ore sono? Sono le …; Quando?; Venerdì, alle dieci mangio/bevo …; Lunedì, studio inglese

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C01-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving reasons for likes and dislikes, for example, Mi piace guardare la TV. È divertente.; Non mi piace studiare. È noioso.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT4C02 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: participate in activities that involve expressing interests and exchanging information, using a range of familiar phrases and modelled structures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C02-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using informal language to create invitations for a performance or class event, for example, Caro … Vieni alla nostra festa/recita/riunione! Il giorno … Alle ore … Luogo/Presso …

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C02-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: working in pairs or small groups to generate questions when preparing for a surprise party, for example, Quanti …?; A che ora?; Dov’è la festa?

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C02-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a real or imagined visit to a local market to buy ingredients for making an Italian dish together such as il minestrone

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C02-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in ordering food at the school canteen, for example, Io prendo un panino con il formaggio. E tu, cosa prendi?

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C02-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: following procedures and instructions together, for example, following recipes such as una macedonia di frutta, or making a model of an Italian garden or piazza

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C02-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in organising a shared lunch in the Italian class, discussing who will make/bring what, for example, Facciamo un dolce; Chi porta lo zucchero?; Chi porta le mele?

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C02-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning for a shared performance for an assembly or guests, for example, Chi dobbiamo invitare?; Facciamo un poster; Cosa facciamo?; Cantiamo una canzone italiana!

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT4C05 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts using formulaic expressions, simple phrases and sentences and modelled textual conventions

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C05-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating or ordering a sequence based on a set of images with captions (e.g. Il papà si alza. Il papà mangia. Il papà parte.) or a known storyline such as ‘La tartaruga e la lepre’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C05-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing messages to their favourite character in a story or children’s television program, for example, Mi piace / Non mi piace la canzone / il quadro; Il documentario è interessante

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C05-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using mime, movement or drama to give expression to events in texts, for example, acting out scenes from a story and taking the role of a character

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C05-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating simple sentences in the subject+verb+object pattern, and playing a game of ‘making silly sentences’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C05-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing and illustrating simple narratives in print or digital format, selecting from modelled language structures and banks of Italian expressions and idioms, for example, a day in the life of a character from a known story or from their imagination

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C05-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a personal profile or a ‘Wanted’ poster using simple words and expressions selected from word banks and modelled statements, highlighting key characteristics and features, for example, Sono australiano di origine greca. Sono bravo e sportivo. Parlo inglese e studio italiano

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C05-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating short oral, digital or print presentations on topics such as holidays, favourite computer games or favourite playground, using a combination of language and images (e.g. photos, illustrations, captions, diagrams), to share with the class

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C05-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading or viewing well-known stories and commenting on the characters, discussing reasons and consequences, for example, Pinocchio è disobbediente; la fata è gentile

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C05-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a print or electronic brochure or infographic for the class to share information (e.g. reasons to visit Italy; the importance of playing sport or eating healthily)

as_extracts.name: LITAF104-E02

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C05-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using mime, movement or drama to give expression to events in texts, for example, acting out scenes from a story and taking the role of a character

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C05-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating simple sentences in the subject+verb+object pattern, and playing a game of ‘making silly sentences’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C05-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing and illustrating simple narratives in print or digital format, selecting from modelled language structures and banks of Italian expressions and idioms, for example, a day in the life of a character from a known story or from their imagination

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C05-E07 - Italian

elaborations.name: VC2LIT4C05-E09 - Italian
