content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10CM03 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: use spoken and written exchanges to discuss, plan and reflect on activities, events and experiences with peers

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM03-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: obtaining information by using appropriate interrogatives (e.g. Chi …?; Quando …?; Come …?; Perché?; Quale?)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM03-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: inviting and responding to invitations, for example, Puoi venire a …? No, devo studiare / Non ora.; Oggi …; A presto.; Divertiti!

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM03-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using gestures and facial expressions to convey meaning and reinforce spoken languages, for example, Vieni qua!; Di là, non da quella parte!; State fermi!

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM03-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in planning and decision-making with others, for example, arranging an event, class debate, performance, excursion or guest speaker, or organising a petition or a letter to the principal or local council, for example, Devo/Dobbiamo organizzare …; Cosa dobbiamo fare?; Chi invitiamo? Bisogna + infinitive; Vuoi venire al dibattito con me?; Come possiamo convincere il comune a …?; Scriviamo una lettera per convincere il/la preside a …

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM03-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating options (e.g. Forse potremmo cominciare alle 7; Potrebbe essere utile andare tutti insieme) and reflecting on outcomes (e.g. È andato tutto bene; È stato un gran successo; Ci siamo riusciti!; Ce l’abbiamo fatta!; La prossima volta forse)

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10CM05 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to interpret and respond to non-verbal, spoken and written interactions and produce texts to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating and discussing idiomatic expressions in both Italian and English, such as Non vedo l’ora! (I can’t wait!), Era ora! (Finally! / It was about time!), Lasciami stare! (Leave me alone!), Ma dai! (Come on!) and Tocca ferro (Touch wood)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing clips where gesture and body language are prominent, first without sound to predict verbal interactions

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising using body language and gesture to aid understanding, for example, miming a story for their peers to summarise in writing

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring, expanding and consolidating word usage, using online applications relating to idioms, proverbs, sayings and set phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing different translations of the same message in Italian and English, for example, Devo scappare/andare/correre can be translated as ‘I must / have to run/go’ or ‘I’ve got to run/go’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the appropriateness of language choices for a given context and purpose according to age, relationship and gender

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing different translations of a text, including versions created by online translation software, and discussing any issues that emerge

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using print and digital dictionaries, selecting appropriate meanings from alternatives provided and comparing translations with their peers, and explaining cultural references and expressions such as fuori (literally, ‘outside’, meaning ‘out of your mind’) or su di giri (literally, ‘revved up’, meaning ‘excitable' or ‘elated’) and any aspects that are lost in translation

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating texts (e.g. public signs) and explaining choices in different renderings such as Non calpestare l’erba (Keep off the grass / Don’t walk on the lawn / Don’t trample the grass)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining visual symbols and signs (e.g. road signs, warnings, directions) in written and spoken Italian

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10CM06 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts, selecting vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and textual conventions for familiar and some unfamiliar contexts and purposes, to engage different audiences

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a different version of a well-known story, changing aspects such as the location, time setting, tense, text type or ending, and publishing it in the school magazine

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing poems, letters or emails to characters from a story or film that has left a significant impression

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: entertaining others by creating texts expressing real or imagined experiences, ideas and emotions, for example, a rap song about being young, a video about a fictional school, a cartoon about a real or fictitious hero, or a short story about an inanimate object coming to life

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a video or a role-play to demonstrate the use of idiomatic expressions in context, such as chatting with a friend (e.g. In gamba!; Figurati!; Permesso …), being a teacher leading an excursion (e.g. Non farmi fare brutta figura!; Gambe in spalla!), or explaining what is wrong (e.g. Ho sete; Ho una fame da lupi)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing to the editor of a print or online newspaper about an event, justifying their personal opinions, or promoting awareness of an issue such as recycling, conservation, sustainability, healthy food choices, or sport and fitness options

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a poster, blog or advertisement using compound sentences (e.g. Mi piace la pizza ma preferisco le lasagne) and complex sentences (e.g. La città che ho visitato era bellissima)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: encouraging people to choose a specific location for a future trip by writing an account of your last holiday there, using persuasive language and imagery

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a journal entry or a contribution for a school newsletter in Italian, reflecting on a visit to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, and, with permission, referring to cultural knowledge of the site’s significance

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: making a ‘pros and cons’ list for continuing the study of Italian in the senior years of school, and then writing an evaluative report for the school newspaper

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a print or digital advertisement or travel brochure in Italian for travel to an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, including what to see and do, traditional and/or cultural considerations, means of travel, best time of year to visit, what to bring and what to wear

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10UL01 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: apply features and conventions of spoken Italian to enhance and extend fluency, and to respond to and create a range of texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the differences in the pronunciation and stress of words with similar spelling, for example, subito/subito when playing a game of tombola, using words with different pronunciation and stress

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using some common interjections (e.g. Oh!; Eh?; Cioè; Ahimè; Ohimè; Uffa!) in cloze and gap-filling exercises, or in whole-class group responses, including selecting the correct expression from a range of flashcards

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and contrasting the pronunciation of similar-sounding words using text-to-speech software or the audio option in word-processing programs

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising common cognates in speech (e.g. organizzazione, programmare, arrivare), and comparing the similarities and differences between spelling in Italian and in other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and interpreting sounds and textual features and devices (e.g. onomatopoeia, repetition, simile, metaphor), and understanding how they can be used to express emotion and convey attitudes

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the difference between anglicised and Italian pronunciations in words such as hamburger, bruschetta, spaghetti and caffellatte

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10UL02 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of context and grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts that include some complex structures, ideas and conventions appropriate to formality and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying the rules for including or omitting the article (e.g. mio padre / il mio papà; Buongiorno signora … / È la signora …), for example, by proofreading short written introductions of people and/or labelling pictures of these people with captions

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing, comparing and reflecting on the use of singular and plural in Italian, English and other known languages, demonstrating awareness that some nouns have irregular plurals (e.g. la città / le città; il dito / le dita) and some are collective nouns (e.g. la gente); classifying nouns from a text as singular or plural; and completing a similar classification for their equivalents in English

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the use of the possessive, reflexive, demonstrative and relative pronouns by eliminating repetition of nouns from written texts, for example, rephrasing spoken language from their peers, the teacher or video clips, by replacing nouns with pronouns

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: making descriptions more precise by using (regular and irregular) comparatives and superlatives, for example, Il film è più bello del romanzo; È bellissimo

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating destinations and directions by using simple or articulated prepositions, for example, in Italia; a Roma; al parco

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a wide range of verb forms in response to visual cues, indicating actions in the present (including irregular and reflexive verbs) and across time (i.e. present perfect, imperfect, future and conditional in modelled contexts)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using the impersonal si and the function of modal verbs to indicate ability, willingness or necessity

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using compound sentences (e.g. Mi piace la pizza ma preferisco le lasagne) and complex sentences (e.g. La città che ho visitato era bellissima)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using idiomatic expressions with fare and avere, for example, Ho fame/sete; Avevo sete; Non ho mai avuto fame come oggi; Avevo fame e così ho mangiato un panino; Ho paura; Ho avuto paura così non mi sono tuffato nell’acqua; Avevo paura del buio

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using adverbs of time and manner, such as ieri and lentamente, to rewrite short texts where these have been omitted

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E11 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the elements that create coherence at a whole-text level, such as the use of cohesive devices, linked paragraphs, and sequencing of ideas (e.g. perché; quindi; siccome; dato che), and using these to write a text about a holiday, a typical school day or an excursion

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: making a ‘pros and cons’ list for continuing the study of Italian in the senior years of school, and then writing an evaluative report for the school newspaper

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a print or digital advertisement or travel brochure in Italian for travel to an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, including what to see and do, traditional and/or cultural considerations, means of travel, best time of year to visit, what to bring and what to wear

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10UL01 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: apply features and conventions of spoken Italian to enhance and extend fluency, and to respond to and create a range of texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the differences in the pronunciation and stress of words with similar spelling, for example, subito/subito when playing a game of tombola, using words with different pronunciation and stress

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using some common interjections (e.g. Oh!; Eh?; Cioè; Ahimè; Ohimè; Uffa!) in cloze and gap-filling exercises, or in whole-class group responses, including selecting the correct expression from a range of flashcards

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and contrasting the pronunciation of similar-sounding words using text-to-speech software or the audio option in word-processing programs

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising common cognates in speech (e.g. organizzazione, programmare, arrivare), and comparing the similarities and differences between spelling in Italian and in other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and interpreting sounds and textual features and devices (e.g. onomatopoeia, repetition, simile, metaphor), and understanding how they can be used to express emotion and convey attitudes

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the difference between anglicised and Italian pronunciations in words such as hamburger, bruschetta, spaghetti and caffellatte

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10UL02 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of context and grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts that include some complex structures, ideas and conventions appropriate to formality and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying the rules for including or omitting the article (e.g. mio padre / il mio papà; Buongiorno signora … / È la signora …), for example, by proofreading short written introductions of people and/or labelling pictures of these people with captions

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing, comparing and reflecting on the use of singular and plural in Italian, English and other known languages, demonstrating awareness that some nouns have irregular plurals (e.g. la città / le città; il dito / le dita) and some are collective nouns (e.g. la gente); classifying nouns from a text as singular or plural; and completing a similar classification for their equivalents in English

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the use of the possessive, reflexive, demonstrative and relative pronouns by eliminating repetition of nouns from written texts, for example, rephrasing spoken language from their peers, the teacher or video clips, by replacing nouns with pronouns

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: making descriptions more precise by using (regular and irregular) comparatives and superlatives, for example, Il film è più bello del romanzo; È bellissimo

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating destinations and directions by using simple or articulated prepositions, for example, in Italia; a Roma; al parco

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a wide range of verb forms in response to visual cues, indicating actions in the present (including irregular and reflexive verbs) and across time (i.e. present perfect, imperfect, future and conditional in modelled contexts)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using the impersonal si and the function of modal verbs to indicate ability, willingness or necessity

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using compound sentences (e.g. Mi piace la pizza ma preferisco le lasagne) and complex sentences (e.g. La città che ho visitato era bellissima)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using idiomatic expressions with fare and avere, for example, Ho fame/sete; Avevo sete; Non ho mai avuto fame come oggi; Avevo fame e così ho mangiato un panino; Ho paura; Ho avuto paura così non mi sono tuffato nell’acqua; Avevo paura del buio

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using adverbs of time and manner, such as ieri and lentamente, to rewrite short texts where these have been omitted

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E11 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the elements that create coherence at a whole-text level, such as the use of cohesive devices, linked paragraphs, and sequencing of ideas (e.g. perché; quindi; siccome; dato che), and using these to write a text about a holiday, a typical school day or an excursion

as_extracts.name: LITA71010-E08
as_extracts.description: They discuss the structures and features of Italian texts using metalanguage.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10UL03 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: reflect on and evaluate Italian texts, using metalanguage to discuss language structures and features

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL03-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing a metalanguage for discussing ideas, issues and experiences related to intercultural communication, such as discussing and using polite forms of pronouns and verbs, for example, La ringrazio; ArriverederLa

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL03-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing grammatical structures, for example, relative clauses, relative pronouns and demonstrative adjectives, using metalanguage to be able to choose between chi and che

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL03-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing procedural, informative and persuasive texts (e.g. recipes, advertisements, weather reports) in Italian, English and/or other languages, using metalanguage to describe their similarities and differences

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL03-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing changes in style, lexicon and grammatical structures, observing how the same facts may be communicated differently by different people in different contexts, for example, describing a school assignment, Non sono stato/a promosso/a; Sono stato/a bocciato/a

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL03-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using metalanguage to discuss the differences between ways of communicating in Italian and English and/or other languages, which involve cultural dimensions (e.g. Sono stato rimandato a settembre, ho la media del 7; Ho fatto forca; mangiare alla mensa; il rientro) or respectful/polite language choices (e.g. Mi scusi / Scusa; S’accomodi / Accomodati)

as_extracts.name: LITA71010-E09
as_extracts.description: They reflect on their own language use and cultural identity, and draw on their experience of learning Italian, to discuss how this influences their ideas and ways of communicating.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10UL04 - Italian
content_descriptions.text: reflect on and explain how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), beliefs, attitudes and values, and how these affect ways of communicating
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the use of dialects or language variations within the context of Italian-speaking communities, and reflecting on how these shape identity and group belonging

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noting changes over time in levels of formality in Italian, particularly in spoken Italian, for example, noting the use of tu/Lei compared with voi/Loro in older texts and regional dialects

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the link between language and cultural values and practices evident in Italy, for example, the appreciation of things of beauty and style expressed by the concept of la bella figura, or the connotations of the concept of mammone

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing how language and culture convey values such as respect, for example, Cosa ne pensi?; Sei d’accordo?; È giusto?; In Australia invece, …; A differenza di …, and practising this in different contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing and discussing the interconnected nature of the linguistic and cultural diversity of Italian-speaking communities, and how this is also relevant to the linguistic and cultural diversity in Australia, including that of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on being a communicator and user of Italian in a variety of social situations, for example, interactions with the sales assistant in a retail setting; saying Permesso when entering a private residence; handshakes or kisses as a greeting, for example, adopting a role in the classroom, and then moving around and greeting people according to their role

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing examples of traditional and contemporary images or texts in print and online, and comparing how representations of identity and gender in the language have changed over time

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and/or reading examples of an Acknowledgement of Country or Place in Italian and creating their own version that names the local Country or Place for an Italian-speaking audience

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: considering how their own and others’ identity may shift according to place and time, discussing cultural notions of ‘self’ as public or private, and noticing the adjustments made according to people and setting, for example, Con la mia famiglia sono …; Mentre online cerco di essere …; Quando ero piccolo ero abbastanza …, ma adesso che sono più grande …

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on and learning to navigate aspects of Italian language and culture such as taboo topics, personal space and perceptions of image, and considering what is ‘acceptable’, for example, È permesso parlare di politca/religione?; Quando?; Con chi?; Perché no?; Si fa? Non si fa.

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10CM01 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: initiate and sustain interactions in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts to exchange ideas, experiences and opinions about their own and others’ personal worlds

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM01-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing experiences and describing events, for example, Ogni anno/weekend …,; Per il mio compleanno voglio …,

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM01-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing hopes and ambitions, and giving reasons for plans (e.g. Penso di + infinitive; Mi piacerebbe + infinitive), for example, speaking in a class talking circle, starting with the conditional (e.g. Vorrei fare l'avvocato; Mi piacerebbe passare un anno in Italia); writing a journal entry about future ambitions (using the future tense or conditional mood); or writing a journal entry dated 10 years in the future (using the present tense)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM01-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recounting personal experiences and expressing opinions through a range of texts, using present and past tenses as appropriate, for example, sharing information about their family history or discussing generational influences (e.g. Ammiro Giovanni perché è venuto in Australia da solo quando aveva diciotto anni)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM01-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: watching a clip where Italian students discuss which subjects they enjoy or do not enjoy, completing a table, and then discussing what they learned and sharing opinions, using a range of expressions, for example, Preferisco …, e tu?; E tu, cosa pensi? Sono d’accordo con te/lei …; Sei d’accordo?; Non mi interessa

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM01-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: contrasting and comparing views on particular expectations and issues (e.g. the use of social media at school) by writing blogs, emails and letters, for example, Sono/Non sono d’accordo; Vorrei dire la mia opinione

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM01-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: showing a photo or an image, and presenting information about past experiences and significant events such as holidays, special events and travel, for example, L'anno scorso …,; Prima siamo andati …; Poi abbiamo fatto …; Dopo …; Infine …; Mi sono divertito/a; Faceva caldo; C'era tanta gente …

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM01-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in reflections and evaluations of classroom experiences, for example, Perché / Come mai …?; È giusto?; Secondo te, …?; Forse …; Dal mio punto di vista, …; A mio avviso, …; Penso che sia …; Sono sicuro che …; È chiaro che …

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM01-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to students talking about their own preferences in classroom presentations or in video clips, and using checklists or notes to collate the results in a survey

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10CM02 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use Italian language in exchanges to question, offer ideas and opinions, negotiate, compare and discuss

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM02-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using communication strategies such as questioning further, or asking for repetition or clarification (e.g. Scusi, non ho capito; Puoi/potresti ripetere?; Puoi aiutarmi a + infinitive?; Come andremo al museo, in treno o in autobus?; Ho capito bene?; Vuoi dire che il venerdì cambiamo aula?), for example, when discussing changes of plans for an excursion, a room change, a timetable swap or a test schedule

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM02-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in negotiations, conversation and correspondence (e.g. discussing travel possibilities to Italy, or the purchase of fashion items, musical equipment or a mobile phone), using relevant vocabulary and grammar, for example, Quanto costa il biglietto per …?; Vorrei il biglietto più economico.; Posso vedere l’ultimo modello del telefonino/cellulare? Ha una custodia colorata?; Queste scarpe sono piccole. Ho bisogno di un numero più grande.; I pantaloni sono troppo larghi. C’è la taglia più piccola?

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM02-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying for a part-time job and participating in a mock interview (il colloquio), using appropriate words, for example, il posto fisso; fare domanda di lavoro; Vorrei fare domanda per il lavoro di cassiera; È commesso/a presso …

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM02-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: requesting a service such as changing a flight, exchanging currency, purchasing a SIM card or confirming accommodation

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM02-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: corresponding to express a complaint, formally and informally, about a poor-quality service, comparing it to other services and suggesting a way to improve, for example, Ti aspetto da più di mezz’ora! Non va bene!; L’avviso che l’aria condizionata non funziona e bisogna chiamare il tecnico / l'idraulico. La finestra non si apre.

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10CM03 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: use spoken and written exchanges to discuss, plan and reflect on activities, events and experiences with peers

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM03-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: obtaining information by using appropriate interrogatives (e.g. Chi …?; Quando …?; Come …?; Perché?; Quale?)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM03-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: inviting and responding to invitations, for example, Puoi venire a …? No, devo studiare / Non ora.; Oggi …; A presto.; Divertiti!

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM03-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using gestures and facial expressions to convey meaning and reinforce spoken languages, for example, Vieni qua!; Di là, non da quella parte!; State fermi!

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM03-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in planning and decision-making with others, for example, arranging an event, class debate, performance, excursion or guest speaker, or organising a petition or a letter to the principal or local council, for example, Devo/Dobbiamo organizzare …; Cosa dobbiamo fare?; Chi invitiamo? Bisogna + infinitive; Vuoi venire al dibattito con me?; Come possiamo convincere il comune a …?; Scriviamo una lettera per convincere il/la preside a …

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM03-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating options (e.g. Forse potremmo cominciare alle 7; Potrebbe essere utile andare tutti insieme) and reflecting on outcomes (e.g. È andato tutto bene; È stato un gran successo; Ci siamo riusciti!; Ce l’abbiamo fatta!; La prossima volta forse)

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Mediating meaning in and between languages
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10CM04 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: interpret and evaluate information, ideas and perspectives in a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts and respond appropriately to context, purpose and audience
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM04-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, viewing or reading texts that depict aspects of Italian culture, art, history or geography, and sharing the information with others, for example, comparing online tourist brochures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM04-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a series of advertisements, taking guided notes, and then creating their own advertisement or brochure to attract Italian tourists to an Australian city/town/area

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM04-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: conducting online surveys to report on attitudes about topics such as water usage, consumer choice, technology use, music or celebrities, and reporting on the findings

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM04-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or reading an article or interview of a well-known Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander person and discussing their opinions and ideas in Italian, and creating and presenting their personal profile to the class

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM04-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating data within a text (e.g. career aspirations for Italian youth) and organising the data in a graph, for example, Il 15% degli intervistati vorrebbe diventare ingegnere informatico / programmatore / attore / cantante

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM04-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching, recording and synthesising information from texts (e.g. television programs, reports, interviews, video clips, documentaries, graffiti, social networks, tables, concept maps, webbing, charts) using checklists, guided note-taking, Venn diagrams, sketches and symbols

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM04-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: organising, ordering and collating information, and presenting findings to an audience in spoken or written form

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM04-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reporting on current events and topics related to personal worlds, through reports, summaries, biographies or journal entries (e.g. presenting a profile of a favourite artist or a famous person), or reporting the findings of a survey (e.g. on languages spoken at home in Australia), for example, Il documentario presenta la storia di …; L’articolo parla di … / rappresenta il punto di vista di …; Lo scrittore pensa …; La maggior parte/maggioranza di / la parte minore/minoranza di / il 20 per cento delle persone + verb …; Entrambi, tutti/pochi studiano ogni sera; A differenza di, però …; Il dépliant australiano sottolinea di più …

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM04-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting and presenting information showing varying perspectives, such as by adopting different roles in a role-play (e.g. child/adult, Australian/Italian, insider/outsider, rural/urban) using present, past and future tenses as appropriate, for example, L’importanza degli spazi pubblici per la vita sociale; La piazza è il cuore della città / il centro commerciale; la passeggiata e la domenica italiana; slow food vs. fast food; la cura dell’ambiente e il riciclaggio; il senso civico; Made in Italy and Made in Australia; milestone birthdays, such as 18 and 21

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM04-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing and using tone, gestures and body language to interpret/support meaning-making, for example, viewing gestures in action, creating a script for a role-play or video that takes account of cultural differences between gestures and body language in Italian and English

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10CM05 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to interpret and respond to non-verbal, spoken and written interactions and produce texts to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating and discussing idiomatic expressions in both Italian and English, such as Non vedo l’ora! (I can’t wait!), Era ora! (Finally! / It was about time!), Lasciami stare! (Leave me alone!), Ma dai! (Come on!) and Tocca ferro (Touch wood)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing clips where gesture and body language are prominent, first without sound to predict verbal interactions

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising using body language and gesture to aid understanding, for example, miming a story for their peers to summarise in writing

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring, expanding and consolidating word usage, using online applications relating to idioms, proverbs, sayings and set phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing different translations of the same message in Italian and English, for example, Devo scappare/andare/correre can be translated as ‘I must / have to run/go’ or ‘I’ve got to run/go’

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the appropriateness of language choices for a given context and purpose according to age, relationship and gender

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing different translations of a text, including versions created by online translation software, and discussing any issues that emerge

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using print and digital dictionaries, selecting appropriate meanings from alternatives provided and comparing translations with their peers, and explaining cultural references and expressions such as fuori (literally, ‘outside’, meaning ‘out of your mind’) or su di giri (literally, ‘revved up’, meaning ‘excitable' or ‘elated’) and any aspects that are lost in translation

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating texts (e.g. public signs) and explaining choices in different renderings such as Non calpestare l’erba (Keep off the grass / Don’t walk on the lawn / Don’t trample the grass)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM05-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining visual symbols and signs (e.g. road signs, warnings, directions) in written and spoken Italian

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10CM06 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts, selecting vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and textual conventions for familiar and some unfamiliar contexts and purposes, to engage different audiences

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a different version of a well-known story, changing aspects such as the location, time setting, tense, text type or ending, and publishing it in the school magazine

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing poems, letters or emails to characters from a story or film that has left a significant impression

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: entertaining others by creating texts expressing real or imagined experiences, ideas and emotions, for example, a rap song about being young, a video about a fictional school, a cartoon about a real or fictitious hero, or a short story about an inanimate object coming to life

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a video or a role-play to demonstrate the use of idiomatic expressions in context, such as chatting with a friend (e.g. In gamba!; Figurati!; Permesso …), being a teacher leading an excursion (e.g. Non farmi fare brutta figura!; Gambe in spalla!), or explaining what is wrong (e.g. Ho sete; Ho una fame da lupi)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing to the editor of a print or online newspaper about an event, justifying their personal opinions, or promoting awareness of an issue such as recycling, conservation, sustainability, healthy food choices, or sport and fitness options

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a poster, blog or advertisement using compound sentences (e.g. Mi piace la pizza ma preferisco le lasagne) and complex sentences (e.g. La città che ho visitato era bellissima)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: encouraging people to choose a specific location for a future trip by writing an account of your last holiday there, using persuasive language and imagery

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a journal entry or a contribution for a school newsletter in Italian, reflecting on a visit to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, and, with permission, referring to cultural knowledge of the site’s significance

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: making a ‘pros and cons’ list for continuing the study of Italian in the senior years of school, and then writing an evaluative report for the school newspaper

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10CM06-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a print or digital advertisement or travel brochure in Italian for travel to an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, including what to see and do, traditional and/or cultural considerations, means of travel, best time of year to visit, what to bring and what to wear

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10UL01 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply features and conventions of spoken Italian to enhance and extend fluency, and to respond to and create a range of texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the differences in the pronunciation and stress of words with similar spelling, for example, subito/subito when playing a game of tombola, using words with different pronunciation and stress

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using some common interjections (e.g. Oh!; Eh?; Cioè; Ahimè; Ohimè; Uffa!) in cloze and gap-filling exercises, or in whole-class group responses, including selecting the correct expression from a range of flashcards

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and contrasting the pronunciation of similar-sounding words using text-to-speech software or the audio option in word-processing programs

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising common cognates in speech (e.g. organizzazione, programmare, arrivare), and comparing the similarities and differences between spelling in Italian and in other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and interpreting sounds and textual features and devices (e.g. onomatopoeia, repetition, simile, metaphor), and understanding how they can be used to express emotion and convey attitudes

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL01-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the difference between anglicised and Italian pronunciations in words such as hamburger, bruschetta, spaghetti and caffellatte

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10UL02 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of context and grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts that include some complex structures, ideas and conventions appropriate to formality and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying the rules for including or omitting the article (e.g. mio padre / il mio papà; Buongiorno signora … / È la signora …), for example, by proofreading short written introductions of people and/or labelling pictures of these people with captions

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing, comparing and reflecting on the use of singular and plural in Italian, English and other known languages, demonstrating awareness that some nouns have irregular plurals (e.g. la città / le città; il dito / le dita) and some are collective nouns (e.g. la gente); classifying nouns from a text as singular or plural; and completing a similar classification for their equivalents in English

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the use of the possessive, reflexive, demonstrative and relative pronouns by eliminating repetition of nouns from written texts, for example, rephrasing spoken language from their peers, the teacher or video clips, by replacing nouns with pronouns

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: making descriptions more precise by using (regular and irregular) comparatives and superlatives, for example, Il film è più bello del romanzo; È bellissimo

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating destinations and directions by using simple or articulated prepositions, for example, in Italia; a Roma; al parco

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a wide range of verb forms in response to visual cues, indicating actions in the present (including irregular and reflexive verbs) and across time (i.e. present perfect, imperfect, future and conditional in modelled contexts)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using the impersonal si and the function of modal verbs to indicate ability, willingness or necessity

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using compound sentences (e.g. Mi piace la pizza ma preferisco le lasagne) and complex sentences (e.g. La città che ho visitato era bellissima)

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using idiomatic expressions with fare and avere, for example, Ho fame/sete; Avevo sete; Non ho mai avuto fame come oggi; Avevo fame e così ho mangiato un panino; Ho paura; Ho avuto paura così non mi sono tuffato nell’acqua; Avevo paura del buio

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using adverbs of time and manner, such as ieri and lentamente, to rewrite short texts where these have been omitted

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL02-E11 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the elements that create coherence at a whole-text level, such as the use of cohesive devices, linked paragraphs, and sequencing of ideas (e.g. perché; quindi; siccome; dato che), and using these to write a text about a holiday, a typical school day or an excursion

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10UL03 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: reflect on and evaluate Italian texts, using metalanguage to discuss language structures and features

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL03-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing a metalanguage for discussing ideas, issues and experiences related to intercultural communication, such as discussing and using polite forms of pronouns and verbs, for example, La ringrazio; ArriverederLa

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL03-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing grammatical structures, for example, relative clauses, relative pronouns and demonstrative adjectives, using metalanguage to be able to choose between chi and che

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL03-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing procedural, informative and persuasive texts (e.g. recipes, advertisements, weather reports) in Italian, English and/or other languages, using metalanguage to describe their similarities and differences

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL03-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing changes in style, lexicon and grammatical structures, observing how the same facts may be communicated differently by different people in different contexts, for example, describing a school assignment, Non sono stato/a promosso/a; Sono stato/a bocciato/a

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL03-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: using metalanguage to discuss the differences between ways of communicating in Italian and English and/or other languages, which involve cultural dimensions (e.g. Sono stato rimandato a settembre, ho la media del 7; Ho fatto forca; mangiare alla mensa; il rientro) or respectful/polite language choices (e.g. Mi scusi / Scusa; S’accomodi / Accomodati)

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LIT10UL04 - Italian
substrand_content_descriptions.text: reflect on and explain how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), beliefs, attitudes and values, and how these affect ways of communicating
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E01 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the use of dialects or language variations within the context of Italian-speaking communities, and reflecting on how these shape identity and group belonging

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E02 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: noting changes over time in levels of formality in Italian, particularly in spoken Italian, for example, noting the use of tu/Lei compared with voi/Loro in older texts and regional dialects

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E03 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the link between language and cultural values and practices evident in Italy, for example, the appreciation of things of beauty and style expressed by the concept of la bella figura, or the connotations of the concept of mammone

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E04 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing how language and culture convey values such as respect, for example, Cosa ne pensi?; Sei d’accordo?; È giusto?; In Australia invece, …; A differenza di …, and practising this in different contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E05 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing and discussing the interconnected nature of the linguistic and cultural diversity of Italian-speaking communities, and how this is also relevant to the linguistic and cultural diversity in Australia, including that of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E06 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on being a communicator and user of Italian in a variety of social situations, for example, interactions with the sales assistant in a retail setting; saying Permesso when entering a private residence; handshakes or kisses as a greeting, for example, adopting a role in the classroom, and then moving around and greeting people according to their role

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E07 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing examples of traditional and contemporary images or texts in print and online, and comparing how representations of identity and gender in the language have changed over time

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E08 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and/or reading examples of an Acknowledgement of Country or Place in Italian and creating their own version that names the local Country or Place for an Italian-speaking audience

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E09 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: considering how their own and others’ identity may shift according to place and time, discussing cultural notions of ‘self’ as public or private, and noticing the adjustments made according to people and setting, for example, Con la mia famiglia sono …; Mentre online cerco di essere …; Quando ero piccolo ero abbastanza …, ma adesso che sono più grande …

elaborations.name: VC2LIT10UL04-E10 - Italian
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on and learning to navigate aspects of Italian language and culture such as taboo topics, personal space and perceptions of image, and considering what is ‘acceptable’, for example, È permesso parlare di politca/religione?; Quando?; Con chi?; Perché no?; Si fa? Non si fa.
